rationale: The core problem — broken state management in local LLM UIs — is a real daily frustration for ML practitioners, but fixing it requires a native desktop application or OS-level daemon that tracks GPU memory state and model file paths across multiple inference processes. This is emphatically NOT buildable with Claude + prompts + a form + Stripe: it requires custom system-level software, GPU driver integration, and distribution infrastructure that a non-technical solo operator cannot ship. Willingness to pay is also weak: this segment heavily skews toward open-source-or-nothing, and no paid substitutes for local LLM session management currently exist at meaningful price points. Drop unless a technical co-founder joins.
solution_plan: This opportunity is not viable for a solo non-technical operator using a Claude-based factory. The fix requires a desktop app or background daemon that hooks into local GPU state — something that needs compiled code, OS-specific installers, and likely AMD ROCm / NVIDIA CUDA integration. There is no honest path to building, selling, or maintaining this with Claude prompts and a landing page. Youval should drop this and not invest further validation time.
